newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Slow Australian stocks soften at open as Dow dips.
newsitem.headline: Slow Australian stocks soften at open as Dow dips.

text.p: A lightly traded Australian share market softened at the opening on Tuesday after interest rate fears again got the better of Wall Street.
The All Ordinaries index shed six points to 2,439.8.
Activity was muted as traders awaited the impact of Tuesday's wage claim verdict from the Australian Industrial Relations Commission and Wednesday's March quarter inflation data.

"New York was down on the back of interest rate fears again," said a Sydney-based dealer, suggesting that losses were likely to be modest as the market awaited today's wage claim verdict and Wednesday's inflation data.
"I wouldn't expect to be down any more than 10 points or so. We are still waiting for some figures."
All the leaders lost a little ground with the exception of CRA which received a mild boost, up four cents at A$19.05 (US$14.86), from the stronger London close of its dual listed sibling, RTZ Plc.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about five to four, while about 47 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
